harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Opened exactly one path through node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD router between lan-a and lan-b): node2 (lan-a, 10.60.1.2) can now reach node3 (lan-b, 10.60.2.2) on TCP/8080 only, with every other flow between the two networks still refused by the default-deny pf ruleset. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time and the configuration/connectivity was proven to survive each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) has vtnet0 on the shared management network and two unassigned NICs, vtnet1 bridged to node2's enp8s0 (lan-a) and vtnet2 bridged to node3's enp8s0 (lan-b), confirmed via ARP MAC match and tcpdump capture.

Assigned OPNsense interfaces opt1 (LANA)=vtnet1=10.60.1.1/24 and opt2 (LANB)=vtnet2=10.60.2.1/24 by editing /conf/config.xml (backed up first) and applying via `configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2`.

Configured static IPs on node2 (10.60.1.2/24) and node3 (10.60.2.2/24) via persistent nmcli connection profiles (NetworkManager was reconciling away raw `ip addr add`), plus specific static routes to the peer subnet via node1's opt1/opt2 IPs, avoiding a duplicate lower-priority default route.

Added a single OPNsense filter rule: pass in on opt1 (lan-a network) proto tcp to 10.60.2.2 port 8080, applied via `configctl filter reload`; verified it rendered in `pfctl -sr` as `pass in quick on vtnet1 ... to 10.60.2.2 port = http-alt`.
Opened tcp/8080 in node3's firewalld (RHEL10), which was independently blocking the destination service regardless of router policy.

Verified functionally: node2->node3:8080 succeeds (HTTP 200); ping node2->node3, node3->node2:8080 (reverse direction), and node2->node3:9090 all fail/timeout, confirming exactly one path is open and nothing else.
Captured baseline boot markers (FreeBSD kern.boottime on node1; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3) plus health evidence (pf rule, interfaces, routes, firewalld ports) before any restart.

Restarted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, polled until exec returned, confirmed kern.boottime changed (16:53:37 -> 16:59:44), and verified opt1/opt2 IPs, the pf pass rule, and ip forwarding all survived.
Ran an end-to-end curl test from node2 to node3:8080 after node1's restart to confirm the path still worked before touching the next node.
Restarted node2 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the static route to 10.60.2.0/24 and TCP/8080 reachability both survived.

Restarted node3 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the static route to 10.60.1.0/24, firewalld's open 8080/tcp port, and full end-to-end reachability (8080 works, ping and 9090 still refused) all survived.
Cleaned up the temporary python http.server test listener on node3.

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology discovery (node2=lan-a, node3=lan-b, node1 between them)
evidence.summary: Confirmed node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 are the unassigned lan-a/lan-b uplinks bridged to node2's and node3's second NIC respectively, distinct from the shared management network.

evidence.requirement: OPNsense default-deny baseline before any change
evidence.summary: config.xml showed no opt1/opt2 interfaces defined yet and pfctl showed a catch-all block-all rule for any unassigned interface traffic.

evidence.requirement: Interface assignment for lan-a (opt1) and lan-b (opt2) on node1
evidence.summary: config.xml mutated to add opt1=vtnet1=10.60.1.1/24 and opt2=vtnet2=10.60.2.1/24, then `configctl interface reconfigure` applied them; ifconfig confirms both interfaces are up with the intended IPs and descriptions LANA/LANB.

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 addressed on lan-a/lan-b with correct routing to the peer subnet
evidence.summary: nmcli persistent profiles set static IPs 10.60.1.2/24 (node2) and 10.60.2.2/24 (node3) plus explicit static routes to the peer /24 via node1, without creating a conflicting default route.

evidence.requirement: Exactly one path opened: node2 -> node3 TCP/8080, all else still refused
evidence.summary: Single pf pass rule for opt1->10.60.2.2:8080/tcp added and confirmed live in pfctl; firewalld on node3 opened for 8080; functional test shows node2->node3:8080 succeeds (HTTP 200) while ping (both directions) and node2->node3:9090 and node3->node2:8080 all fail, proving only the required flow is open.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=16:53:37 captured; `shutdown -r now` acked; exec timed out mid-reboot then returned with kern.boottime=16:59:44 (changed); opt1/opt2 IPs, pf pass rule, and ip forwarding confirmed restored; end-to-end curl to node3:8080 from node2 succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=03408ac4... captured; `systemctl reboot` acked; exec timed out then returned with boot_id=7dbfca00... (changed); static route to 10.60.2.0/24 and TCP/8080 reachability to node3 confirmed restored.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=6ab6a71b... and firewalld port 8080/tcp captured; `systemctl reboot` acked; exec timed out then returned with boot_id=c38d5dd9... (changed); static route to 10.60.1.0/24 and firewalld 8080/tcp confirmed restored, and full end-to-end retest (8080 works, ping/9090 refused) confirmed the required single path survived all three restarts.

attempts.summary: Opened exactly one path through node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD router between lan-a and lan-b): node2 (lan-a, 10.60.1.2) can now reach node3 (lan-b, 10.60.2.2) on TCP/8080 only, with every other flow between the two networks still refused by the default-deny pf ruleset. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time and the configuration/connectivity was proven to survive each restart.
